newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Hanoi investment law changes may disappoint - lawyers.
newsitem.headline: Hanoi investment law changes may disappoint - lawyers.

text.p: Foreign lawyers in Hanoi said on Thursday that proposed amendments to Vietnam's Foreign Investment Law may fail to tackle investors' chief concerns.
"The draft I've seen is a complete disappointment," said one lawyer, who declined to be named. "Clarification of the issues people are interested in aren't there."
Vietnam's Foreign Investment Law came into effect in 1987, shortly after the communist leadership embarked on a drive to reform the command economy and open doors to the outside world.
The law was amended in 1990 and 1992 and is due to be adjusted again after debate in the National Assembly next month.
Lawyers said that, judging from drafts, the proposed amendments were not only limited in scope but also apparently aimed at protecting Vietnamese industry from foreign competition.
"It's protectionism and tinkering more than anything else," said one lawyer. "It's small beer. It's not going to make any difference."
Although foreign investment has been flooding into Vietnam's fast-growing economy in recent years, investors frequently complain about red tape and an inadequate legal and regulatory framework.

A draft of the amendments, a copy of which was obtained by Reuters, showed that under new regulations the government would be required to issue investment licenses and decisions within two months from the date of application instead of three months.
The draft listed several areas where foreign investment would be encouraged, those where it was to be prohibited and those where 100 percent foreign-owned enterprises would be banned.
Telecoms, insurance, auditing and electricity generation and distribution were included in the last of the three categories.
Foreign investment in exploitation of forest products, wood processing, broadcasting, television and cinematography would be banned.
